problem:
Use the flux form of Green's theorem to calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y)=⟨xy-\sqrt{{y}^{2}+1},\,{x}^{3}+y⟩
$$

through the boundary of the triangle with vertices $(0,0),(1,2),$ and $(-1,2).$

feedback.problem:
Use the flux form of Green's theorem to calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y)=⟨x-\sqrt{y},\,y-\sqrt{x}⟩
$$

through the boundary of the region enclosed by the curve $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and the line $y=0$ for $0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $F=P\,i+Q\,j,$ and $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062447/assets/c4dd4d03bdfcf6c3d597e2fdef8681e4f3316b3f276cb9967933b61b0dc90976.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=x-\sqrt{y}$ and $Q(x,y)=y-\sqrt{x}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=1,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D={(x,y):0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le \operatorname{sin}⁡x}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem in flux form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(1+1)\,\text{d}A \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}y\,{|}_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,dx \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,dx \\  & =2(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =2(0-(-1)) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
